subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a design for an armored riot-control interceptor vehicle—boxy wheeled body, roof water cannon turret, neon light bars, corporate branding, and a glow kit—aiming for a static model built with a manageable part count using efficient geometry construction.

Setting up dimensions, colors (gunmetal, armor panels, hazard yellow, neon cyan/magenta, police lights), and a box-helper function for building the chassis, hull, cabin, and slanted windshield.

Now blocking out the hood, rear compartment, roof-mounted turret with a cannon barrel aiming forward with a glowing cyan tip, and the front bull bar with hazard striping.

I'm adding a door emblem via an SVG texture with custom unit markings, plus side armor ribs, mirrors, rear ladders and tank details, a roof sensor dome with glowing red eye, hazard stripe patterns on the bumper, and a skid plate with exhaust detailing.

Now setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders with proper rotation and axis alignment, then starting on the wheel geometry.

I'm reconsidering the hull width versus wheel placement since the wheels would intersect the body—deciding it's fine to let the wheels partially bury into the hull for an armored-pod look, and adding fender flare boxes over each wheel to mask the overlap.

Now I'm laying out the rest of the body: hull extends along z from -2.6 to 2.6 with wheels positioned at z 1.6 and -1.5, then stacking a cabin box above it and starting a windshield panel.

Shaping the hood and sloped windshield, working out rotation angles so the glass tilts backward correctly relative to the cabin front face.

Actually that gap would just reveal the cabin interior behind the slanted glass, so I should fill it with a solid triangular pillar extruded in armor color to cover the space between the hood top and windshield top. Then I'll add dark slabs for side windows on the cabin.

Still placing boxes...

I was considering side water tanks along the rear box but the dimensions kept clashing with wheel placement and overall width, so I'm dropping that idea in favor of simpler side armor slats with a glowing cyan vertical window strip indicating the water level.

Now I'm placing light bars and neon accents: a roof light bar on the cabin alternating red/blue glow segments, underglow cyan strips along the hull sides, a thin magenta stripe, and headlight slits plus a front fascia panel near where the hull ends.

I'm adding the bumper armor, hazard stripe accents, and a push-bar frame with cross bar up front, plus thinking about a hood-mounted display panel with a "CIVIL ORDER" logo texture.

For the back I'm placing a red glow bar, taillights, rear doors, bumper, exhaust pipes, and a ladder, then adding roof details like antennas and a drone sensor dome with a glowing red eye lens, plus side spotlights. I'm also designing the door logo texture as an SVG with a cyan hex outline, "RCU-7" text, a magenta bar, and "CORP SECURITY" lettering to apply as a plane on the doors.

Now I'm working out the exact placement and orientation of that logo plane on each side of the hull, calculating viewer perspective so the text reads correctly front-to-rear from someone standing beside the vehicle.

I'm adding details like a dark hex plate background for readability, hazard stripe skirts, window grills, and side mirrors, then planning to code it all with reusable mirror loops and careful part counts around 150, including wheel lug placement around each rim.

Still writing geometry code...
